input_references.role: Task-linked GPS delivery segments for the same courier

metadata.goal: Analyze how time windows affect the delivery behavior of the same courier using the supplied trajectories.
metadata.category: time-window constraints, network-route efficiency, and delivery speed
metadata.header: Time Windows and One Courier’s Route Execution
metadata.dataset_description: A one-courier case with five daily task sets. It provides delivery event times, optional explicit service windows, network-shortest route distance, realized route distance, and task-linked GPS segments. 59 of 90 tasks (65.6%) have no time window.

insight_list.insight: Narrower promised service windows are associated with higher route detour ratios, indicating more circuitous delivery paths relative to the supplied network-shortest distance.

plot.title: Time-Window Width and Route Detour
plot.description: The full route-detour-ratio distributions show increasingly circuitous paths as constrained windows narrow.

insight_list.question: How does route detour relative to the supplied network-shortest distance vary with promised service-window width?

insight_list.insight: On days when this courier handles a larger share of time-window-constrained tasks, route execution is less efficient and average travel speed is lower than on days dominated by unconstrained tasks.

plot.title: Daily Time-Window Share, Route Efficiency, and Speed
plot.description: Each point is one daily task set; more than 60% of all supplied tasks have no time window.

insight_list.question: How do daily route efficiency and speed change as the share of the courier’s tasks with promised time windows increases?

insight_list.insight: After the main concentration of time-window-constrained tasks, the courier's remaining acceptances become sparse.

plot.title: Sparse Acceptance after the Main Time-Window Task Concentration
plot.description: Daily acceptance timelines distinguish the main constrained-task concentration, occasional later constrained tasks, and the sparse remaining acceptances.

insight_list.question: After the main concentration of time-window-constrained tasks, how many further non-block tasks are accepted later in the day?

insights: Narrower promised service windows are associated with higher route detour ratios, indicating more circuitous delivery paths relative to the supplied network-shortest distance.
On days when this courier handles a larger share of time-window-constrained tasks, route execution is less efficient and average travel speed is lower than on days dominated by unconstrained tasks.
After the main concentration of time-window-constrained tasks, the courier's remaining acceptances become sparse.
summary: For this courier, tighter time windows are associated with more circuitous routes and slower delivery execution. Daily task sets containing more constrained tasks show poorer route efficiency, while acceptance becomes sparse after each day’s main concentration of constrained tasks.
